content: These draft amendments are strategically designed to introduce significant compliance requirements for satellite internet services, directly reflecting the growing importance of stringent regulation in accommodating rapid advancements in satellite technology [56] . The trajectory of these recent developments traces its origins to proposed regulatory changes that were initially introduced as early as May 2026, highlighting the authority’s sustained focus on managing radio frequency spectrum specifically for satellite services. Furthermore, during a parliamentary update on May 15, 2026, ICASA outlined its “Future Overall Agenda on the use of Spectrum,” which provided valuable insight into the authority's forward-looking stance on spectrum utilization, even though specific actions or definitive outcomes since that update remain somewhat unclear [95] . Despite the specificity of these regulatory updates, the explicit characterization of these documents as “draft amendments” indicates that the proposals are still subject to potential revisions or finalization, leaving a degree of uncertainty regarding their current implementation status [94] . Historical references to the Radio Frequency Spectrum Regulations of 2015 highlight the past regulatory frameworks that likely influenced the current amendments, although these older frameworks are now considered outdated and have been largely supplanted by recent legislative efforts to modernize and align regulations with contemporary technological advancements. It is important to note that while the publications from May and June 2026 provide a clear picture of ICASA’s regulatory intentions and initial procedural steps, they do not comprehensively address whether the proposed amendments have been formally enacted or if further refinements have taken place in the interim [72] [56] [94] . Consequently, the spectrum licensing landscape in South Africa appears to be undergoing significant regulatory adjustments targeted at satellite services, but it remains in a transitional phase pending finalization or further official updates from ICASA. For stakeholders and telecommunications entities relying on definitive and finalized information regarding spectrum licensing in South Africa, consulting ICASA’s official communications beyond the June 2026 timeframe will be critical to accurately ascertain the current status of the regulations and their subsequent implementation effects.
